1.text:
It was the morning of the school fun fair, and the hall was buzzing with excitement. Colourful balloons hung from the ceiling, and the smell of popcorn drifted through the air. Mei Ling and her best friend, Priya, had been planning their game stall for weeks.

"Do you think anyone will play our ring toss game?" Priya asked nervously, arranging the bottles in a neat row.

"Of course!" Mei Ling replied with a grin. "We have the best prizes — everyone loves the little plush toys."

Just then, their teacher, Mrs Ong, walked over with a kind smile. "Your stall looks wonderful, girls. Remember to speak loudly and clearly when you welcome the visitors."

Soon, the doors opened and families streamed in. A little boy tugged at his mother's sleeve and pointed at the ring toss. "Mummy, I want to try!"

Mei Ling handed him three rings. "Three tries for one dollar!" she called out cheerfully.

The boy threw the first ring — it bounced off the bottle. The second ring wobbled and fell short. On his third try, the ring sailed through the air and landed neatly around a bottle. The crowd cheered!

"I won! I won!" the boy shouted, jumping up and down with joy. He chose a blue plush toy and hugged it tightly.

By the end of the day, Mei Ling and Priya had raised more money than any other stall. "We did it!" Priya exclaimed. Mrs Ong gave them a thumbs up. "Well done, girls. You make our class proud."
1.title: The School Fun Fair

2.text:
One Saturday morning, Daniel was riding his bicycle home when he saw his elderly neighbour, Mrs Lim, struggling with two heavy bags of groceries at the foot of the stairs.

"Good morning, Mrs Lim!" Daniel called out, hopping off his bicycle. "Let me help you carry those."

"Oh, thank you, Daniel," Mrs Lim said gratefully, wiping the sweat from her forehead. "My knees are not as strong as they used to be."

Daniel took both bags and followed Mrs Lim slowly up the stairs. "Did you buy all this from the market?" he asked.

"Yes, I bought fresh vegetables and fish for dinner," Mrs Lim replied. "My grandchildren are coming to visit tonight, and I want to cook their favourite dishes."

When they reached her door, Mrs Lim unlocked it and smiled. "Come in for a while, Daniel. I made some curry puffs this morning."

Daniel's eyes lit up. "Thank you, Mrs Lim! They smell delicious."

As he munched on a warm curry puff, Daniel asked, "Do your grandchildren visit often?"

Mrs Lim shook her head sadly. "Not as often as I would like. They are busy with school."

Daniel thought for a moment. "I can visit you more often if you like. I can help you carry your groceries every Saturday."

Mrs Lim's face broke into a wide smile. "That would be wonderful, Daniel. You are a kind boy."
2.title: Mrs Lim's Groceries

3.text:
Rain pattered against the window as Siti stared out at the grey sky. It was Saturday afternoon, and she had planned to play badminton with her friends at the park. Now, her plans were ruined.

"It's raining cats and dogs!" her younger brother, Aiman, groaned. "What are we going to do all day?"

Their mother looked up from her book. "Why don't you two help me bake some chocolate chip cookies? It is the perfect weather for baking."

Siti and Aiman exchanged glances and shrugged. "All right," Siti said. "But I get to stir the batter!"

Soon, the kitchen was filled with laughter and the sweet smell of chocolate. Flour dusted the countertop, and Aiman had a smudge of batter on his nose. "You look like a clown!" Siti teased, and they both burst out laughing.

"Be careful not to eat all the chocolate chips before they go into the oven," Mother warned with a smile.

When the cookies were finally ready, the three of them sat by the window with glasses of warm milk. Outside, the rain continued to fall, but inside, it was warm and cosy.

"You know," Siti said thoughtfully, "a rainy afternoon is not so bad after all."

"Especially with cookies," Aiman agreed, reaching for his third one.
3.title: The Rainy Afternoon

4.text:
On his way home from school, Wei Jie found a brown wallet lying on the pavement near the bus stop. He picked it up and looked inside. There were several notes and a student pass with a photo of a boy about his age.

"Someone must be very worried," Wei Jie thought. He looked around, but there was no one nearby.

"Mum, I found a wallet!" Wei Jie said as soon as he reached home.

His mother examined the student pass. "This boy is from the school across the road. We should return it to him."

"But how do we find him?" Wei Jie asked.

"The student pass has his name and class," Mother replied. "We can call his school on Monday."

Wei Jie nodded, but he could not stop thinking about the wallet. What if the boy needed the money urgently? What if it was his lunch money for the whole week?

The next morning, Wei Jie went to the school across the road and handed the wallet to the general office. The kind office lady smiled. "You are an honest boy. The owner came looking for this yesterday. He was very upset."

A few days later, Wei Jie received a thank-you card from the boy. "Thank you for returning my wallet. You are a true friend." Wei Jie smiled proudly. He knew he had done the right thing.
4.title: The Lost Wallet

5.text:
The school hall was packed with parents for the annual class concert. Behind the curtain, the Primary 5 pupils waited nervously in their colourful costumes. Tonight, they would perform a short play about friendship.

"I'm so nervous," whispered Jia Le, peeking through a gap in the curtain. "There are so many people!"

"Don't worry," said his friend, Hui Min, patting his shoulder. "We have practised so many times. We will do fine."

Their teacher, Mr Tan, gathered them in a circle. "Remember, speak loudly and clearly. Most importantly, enjoy yourselves!"

The lights dimmed and the curtain rose. At first, Jia Le's voice trembled, but as the play went on, he grew more confident. The audience laughed at the funny parts and clapped at the songs.

During the final scene, Hui Min forgot her line. For a moment, there was silence. Then Jia Le whispered her line to her, and she continued smoothly. The audience did not even notice.

When the play ended, the whole hall erupted in applause. The pupils bowed, their faces glowing with pride.

"You were wonderful!" Jia Le's mother said afterwards, hugging him tightly. "I am so proud of you."

"It was a team effort," Jia Le replied with a grin. "We helped each other, and that made all the difference."
5.title: The Class Concert

6.text:
Early on Sunday morning, Grandpa took Xiao Ming to the park for a walk. The air was fresh, and the birds were singing in the trees. Dew sparkled on the grass like tiny diamonds.

"Grandpa, look! There is a squirrel!" Xiao Ming exclaimed, pointing at a bushy-tailed squirrel scampering up a tree.

"Shh," Grandpa whispered with a smile. "If you stay quiet, you may see more animals."

They walked slowly along the path and soon came to the pond. A family of ducks glided across the water, followed by five fluffy ducklings.

"The ducklings are following their mother," Xiao Ming observed. "Just like I follow you, Grandpa."

Grandpa chuckled. "That is right. And one day, you will lead the way."

Near the playground, they met an old friend of Grandpa's, Uncle Ravi, who was doing tai chi under a large tree. "Would you like to try?" Uncle Ravi asked Xiao Ming.

Xiao Ming copied the slow, graceful movements, trying hard not to wobble. "This is harder than it looks!" he laughed.

By the time they headed home, the sun was high in the sky. "Thank you for bringing me here, Grandpa," Xiao Ming said. "Can we come again next Sunday?"

"Of course," Grandpa replied. "The park will be waiting for us."
6.title: A Morning in the Park

7.title: The Tortoise and the Eagle
7.text:
A tortoise sat on the ground, raised his head and watched the birds circling in the air above him. He grew dissatisfied with his own life when he saw the birds enjoying themselves in the clear blue sky.

He stared longingly at them, wishing he could join them and share their freedom. "If I can go up into the air, I am sure I can fly just like them," he thought to himself.

He was pondering over this problem when an eagle came to rest on a rock beside him. Taking this opportunity, he approached the eagle and pleaded with him to teach him how to fly. The eagle refused to accede to the request at first for he considered it not only foolish but also impossible.

But the tortoise was persistent. He kept pleading with him. The eagle finally agreed. Clutching the tortoise tightly in its claws, he flew higher and higher.

Having taken the tortoise up to a great height in the air, the tortoise asked to be released. The misguided tortoise found himself falling rapidly through the air. Just as he was about to hit upon a huge rock, the eagle swooped down and saved the silly tortoise from smashing into pieces.

8.title: What Is Gravity?
8.text:
"What is gravity?" asked seven-year-old Nicholas, scratching his head. Then he pointed to the word in a science book he was reading.

"We cannot see it but we would know if it isn't there. We can see its effects on objects around us. If a pen rolls off a table, it will drop to the floor. If a fruit is ripe, it will fall to the ground," Jason tried to explain it to his little brother as simply as he could.

"Yes, everything would float off into space like lost balloons without the earth's gravity tugging them downwards," Janet chipped in.

"Oh, I understand now! It is a kind of force that attracts everyone and everything towards the earth, am I right?" exclaimed Nicholas excitedly.

"Yes, centre of the earth, to be exact," their mother added. "Gravity does more than just keeping people and objects on earth from floating away. It is the earth's gravity that holds the moon as it revolves around the earth. You can do an experiment to show how gravity holds the moon in orbit around the earth," their mother explained patiently. "Get a tennis ball. Tie a string around it securely. Then you take one end of the string and swing it around your head. The tennis ball is likened to the moon and you, the earth. Gravity from the earth is like an invisible piece of string that prevents the moon from flying away from the earth."

9.title: A Game of Bingo
9.text:
Josh invited his friends over to his house one Saturday afternoon. While his friends were chatting among themselves, Josh went to the study and returned with a box in his hands.

"Shall we play a game of Bingo?" Josh suggested. "Does everyone know how to play the game?"

Keith and Linus shook their heads.

"It's really easy. Let us show you how the game is played," Josh suggested. The others nodded their heads in unison.

Josh took out some cards and a bag with numbered balls in it. Then, he passed some circular discs and one card to each of his friends. The card showed 25 squares, each with a number in it.

"The 'caller' will draw a numbered ball from the bag. He has to call out the number that is shown on the ball. If any of the players sees the number on his card, he can cover the number with a circular disc. The caller continues to draw out the numbered balls until one of the players covers a straight line of five numbers on his card. He then shouts 'Bingo' so that the rest of the players know."

"The 'caller' checks to make sure the five numbers have indeed been called. A new game starts again," Stewart added.

"It sounds like great fun!" remarked Keith.

"I agree! Let's get started!" said Linus.

10.title: Joshua's Painting
10.text:
Mrs Turner was thinking about an activity that she could do with her two-year-old son, Joshua. After some research, she hit upon a simple idea and decided to try it out. She prepared big pieces of paper, poster paints and paintbrushes. This activity could help to develop creativity and encourage Joshua to use his imagination.

Mrs Turner did not want to tell Joshua what they were doing that day. He was very curious as he watched his mother dip a paintbrush into a bottle of red paint. Then she reached out for Joshua's hand and pressed the paintbrush onto his palm, painting it red, first one hand and then the other. Joshua giggled as his hands were being painted. It was rather ticklish. He was then encouraged to press his hands on the paper.

He was excited to see the red palm prints on the paper. Mrs Turner asked Joshua if he wanted to use another colour. He chose green. Joshua began to create patterns using his hands as his mother painted them with different colours.

Joshua repeated the activity with his feet. This time, Mrs Turner joined in the fun too. They created a masterpiece and hung it on the wall for Mr Turner to see when he returned home from work.

11.title: Finding the Way by the Stars
11.text:
How do travellers and explorers find their way around unfamiliar lands before the inventions of smart devices and navigation apps? In addition to a great sense of adventure, navigation skill is also very important. Travellers and explorers need to keep track of where they are and the direction in which they are going. This is especially so in the case of open seas or deserts. These places have no landmarks to guide travellers in their journey.

For thousands of years, travellers have used the constellations to help them find their way while travelling from one place to another. These groups of stars in the sky form a pattern or picture which travellers can use as a guide to help them as they move from place to place. Two constellations which are particularly useful are the Little Bear and the Southern Cross. They help travellers to find the direction of north and south. The Little Bear constellation points towards the north and the Southern Cross constellation, which is the brightest of all constellations, is used to find south.

Each constellation is much like a compass in the sky. Once the travellers know where north or south lies, it will not be too difficult for them to work out the other directions.

12.title: The Dodo
12.text:
The dodo, a bird that once lived on the island of Mauritius in the Indian Ocean became extinct around 1690. The dodo was about three feet tall with a big, round body covered in soft feathers. It had short wings and did not fly.

Dodos were known for their friendly and curious nature. When sailors first arrived on the island in the 17th century, the dodos were not particularly afraid of them. Unfortunately, this made them easy prey for the sailors, who hunted them for their meat and eggs. Due to over hunting and changes in the environment, the dodo population decreased quickly. The last dodo was said to be spotted towards the end of the 17th century.

The extinction of the dodo teaches an important lesson about taking care of our environment and the animals that live in it. We should work together to protect the amazing creatures we have in the world so that they do not suffer the same fate as the dodo.

13.title: A Visit to the Fire Station
13.text:
Last Friday, Miss Mabel brought her class for an excursion to the fire station. She wanted her students to see and learn how things are run inside the red brick building and what the firefighters have to do during emergencies. She introduced them to Mr Lee, the commander of the fire station.

Before Mr Lee showed the students around the fire station, there was a short discussion between the students and him. He wondered aloud how much the students knew about the occupation. The students were only too eager to show off what they knew or learnt from school about firefighters. It was evident that they were excited to find out more about what firefighters do besides extinguishing fires and rescuing people. Mr Lee told them a firefighter has to pass many tests before he can be certified as a professional. In addition, a firefighter must be strong and physically fit.

At last, Mr Lee brought the eager students to look at the fire engines. He pointed out to them the hydraulic platform on the fire engine which they use to put out fires in flats or other high-rise buildings. The students jumped when Mr Lee pressed a button on one of the fire engines to let them hear the siren. It was extremely loud! The students also tried out the pole that the firefighters use to slide down from the second level to get to the fire engines speedily.

At the end of the visit, Miss Mabel and her class thanked Mr Lee for the tour. It was a great learning experience for all of them.

14.title: Tom and the River
14.text:
Tom splashed about lazily in the river. It was a warm day. There was no wind and the sun's rays pierced through the clouds, shining on the dry land.

Tom was only a little boy and had not yet learnt to swim. He was happy to float on his back, standing up occasionally to splash water on his body. Unknowingly, he floated to the middle of the river where it was too deep for him. In an instant, he realised that he could not touch the bottom of the river with his feet. He was trying to struggle to safety when he saw a stranger swimming towards him.

"Help me!" he shouted as loudly as he could. "Help me or I will drown!" The stranger caught hold of Tom and swam slowly towards the bank.

"How did you get yourself into such trouble? Surely you must have known that the river is deep at this end? Do your parents know you go into deep waters even though you cannot swim? Now, you are lucky I was passing by here. You should thank your lucky stars ..."

The man went on and on, stopping every now and then to emphasise a point. The poor boy felt he would never reach the bank. Tom finally managed to get to a place where his feet could feel the river bed. He scrambled quickly to the bank, exhausted.

"You could have given me that long lecture after you have got me out of the water! You almost drowned me with your words!" Tom exclaimed in exasperation.

15.title: A Noodle Dish
15.text:
You can cook a simple delicious noodle dish with leftover roast chicken. Follow the instructions below. Ask an adult to help you.

1. Shred the chicken into small pieces. Put aside for now.
2. Proceed to make the sauce for the noodles. Prepare one teaspoon of light soya sauce, one tablespoon of oyster sauce and two tablespoons of oil.
3. Mix the sauce well in a bowl. Then pour the sauce mixture onto a plate. Repeat the same steps for each serving.
4. Boil some water in a pot to cook the noodles. Add your favourite noodles into the water as it begins to boil. Stir gently until the noodles soften.
5. Turn off the stove. You can scoop up the noodles or pour directly into a strainer.
6. Transfer the noodles onto the plate with the sauce you prepared earlier and mix them well. Set aside.
7. Heat one tablespoon of oil in a small wok over medium fire.
8. Fry some shredded ginger with beansprouts or your preferred vegetables for about a minute. Add salt and sugar to taste.
9. Add the shredded roast chicken into the wok and mix well. Turn off the stove.
10. Now, scoop the shredded roast chicken and vegetables onto the noodles.

Your dish is ready to be served!

16.title: How Rainforest Animals Talk
16.text:
Zoo-keeper: Rainforest animals have plenty to talk about. They communicate regularly.

Jessie: That's fascinating! How do these animals talk?

Zoo-keeper: Take the gibbon, for example. It is a musical animal. When a male and a female gibbon mate, they stay as friends forever, performing duets with each other. The more synchronised their duets are, the more attached they are to each other. A family of gibbons also calls across the canopy to keep unfriendly animals away from its patch.

Jessie: I never knew that! What about the proboscis monkeys? Do they sing too?

Zoo-keeper: The male proboscis monkey has a long droopy nose which he 'plays' loudly like a trumpet, making strange honking sounds. He lets the other monkeys in his group know that he is the boss by warning them of impending danger and calling them together to meet.

Jessie: What about frogs? Do they sing too?

Zoo-keeper: All kinds of male frogs serenade to their female counterparts with deep throaty croaks. The male with the loudest croak wins the affection of the female. Frogs also croak to repel other males from their territory.

Jessie: I am intrigued. I will do some research of my own on the internet to learn more about how the other animals communicate.

17.title: Plants Are Useful
17.text:
Plants are very useful to us. Plants provide us with materials, medicine and food.

most of our food and beverages come from plants. Tofu is made from soya beans. Soya milk is extracted from the soya beans after they are soaked and ground. The soya milk is poured into stainless steel trays or soft plastic packages before a thickening substance is added to form tofu.

The cocoa beans from which we make chocolate grow on cacao trees. The beans are actually seeds found in fruit pods. Cacao trees grow in hot and wet places like West Africa.

We have always used plants to keep ourselves well. A foxglove plant is poisonous, but taken in small amounts, the chemicals in its leaves help weak hearts to beat more strongly. Willow trees can cure headaches. Their bark is used to make aspirin tablets. Plant medicines are generally popular among people because they are natural and gentle in healing a human body. Eating dandelion plants helps speed up the flow of water through the body. About half of all the medicines that we use today began as natural plant cures.

As such, the rainforests are important sources of food and healing plants. If we should continue to cut them down, we may lose natural food sources and many drug yielding plants for medicines.

18.title: Earthworms
18.text:
The soil is crawling with earthworms. Some earthworms are tiny and a microscope is needed to see them clearly. Others grow to a few metres.

Earthworms make tunnels by munching through the soil, swallowing tiny bits of decomposed food like vegetables and fruit along the way. As they tunnel in the soil, earthworms bring the bottom soil to the surface, mixing it with the topsoil. As earthworms move along, they secrete slime which contains nitrogen. Plants need nitrogen to grow well. Hence, earthworms play an important role in the growth of plants and trees.

Earthworms excrete their droppings, which are called castings, underground or just outside their tunnels. These droppings are full of goodness as they help to make the soil more fertile, allowing new seedlings to grow in the ground.

Most worms do not live past one year for they have to cope with garden forks and other predators. Shrews, especially, love to eat earthworms, and so do moles. It is common belief that if you cut a worm into two, the two halves can recover and grow into two separate, fully formed worms. however, it is more likely that you will end up having two halves of a dead worm!

19.title: Black Bears
19.text:
A black bear, which is approximately 120 to 150 centimetres tall, actually varies in colour from glossy black to dark brown, reddish-brown or almost white. There is often a small white patch on its chest.

Black bears in the wild are occasionally seen in the day. They roam long distance in search of food such as fruit, berries, nuts and honey. being omnivores, they also feed on insects, other small mammals and fish that have been stranded beside the river. Most black bears go to sleep an hour or two before sunset. There are, however, some which are active at night.

In autumn, black bears feed on the plentiful supplies of fruit, nuts and succulent greens to fatten themselves for their long sleep during the cold weather which can last over seven months. The mating season usually lasts from late May to early July. after mating, the male and female black bears separate.

except for the females with cubs, black bears are usually solitary. Female black bears usually give birth to a litter of one to four young at a time. Cubs usually stay with their mother for about seventeen months before they travel on their own.

20.title: The Air Conditioner
20.text:
The very first air conditioner was invented by Willis Haviland Carrier in 1902. He was an engineer from New York and his invention changed the way we live during the hot months of the year.

Willis Carrier's invention was originally created to solve a specific problem. He was hired by a printing company in Brooklyn, New York. The company's printing process was being ruined by the high humidity in the summer. The paper they used would expand and contract with the changing humidity, causing the ink to smudge and the paper to wrinkle.

to solve this problem, Carrier designed a machine that controlled both temperature and humidity. It used a system of coils and fans to cool and dry the air inside the building. This machine not only helped the printing company but also created a whole new way to stay comfortable in hot weather.

Air conditioners work by taking in warm air, cooling it down by passing it over cold coils and then blowing the cool air back into the room. They also remove moisture from the air, which helps the body feel less 'sticky'. This process makes the indoor environment much more pleasant during hot summer days.

At first, air conditioning was mainly used in big buildings and areas, like movie theatres, department stores and offices. As technology advanced, air conditioners became more affordable and smaller, making them accessible to homes all over the world.

21.title: Chocolate Profiteroles
21.text:
Here is a recipe for chocolate profiteroles with choux pastry.

Choux Pastry

1. Put 90 g of butter and 200 ml of water in a pan. Bring the mixture to a boil slowly.

2. Remove the pan from the heat and sift in the flour before stirring the mixture.

3. Beat the mixture vigorously with a wooden spoon until it comes away from the sides of the pan. Allow the mixture to cool a little.

4. Beat three eggs, then add a little at a time to the mixture, until the mixture is soft, smooth and has a dropping consistency.

5. Put the mixture onto a greased baking sheet. Bake it for twenty-five minutes in the oven that has been preheated at 105 °C. Remove and then leave it to cool.

Chocolate Profiterole

1. Whisk 600 ml of double cream with two tablespoons of icing sugar until it becomes thick and fluffy. Cut a slit in each of the profiteroles and fill them with the sweetened cream.

2. Put 175 g of chocolate in a bowl. Melt it in a microwave for about a minute. After that, add in the butter and allow it to melt. Combine to make a smooth mixture. Leave it to cool.

Chocolate Profiterole With Choux Pastry

Spread a little of the chocolate mixture over the top of each profiterole with a butter knife.

22.title: The Wedding
22.text:
"It's a wedding invitation!" Mrs Bennet exclaimed when she opened the envelope. She read its contents and smiled. "Your cousin, Angela, is getting married and we are all invited!"

"Where is the wedding going to be held?" Alicia asked excitedly as she peeped over her mother's shoulder to see the card.

"We will be witnessing the ceremony at the registry office. It's where a couple goes to register their marriage," Mrs Bennet replied.

A few days later, Mrs Bennet took Alicia and her brother shopping. They bought a wedding gift for the couple. They also chose a card. The children waited patiently while Mrs Bennet wrote a congratulatory message on the card. then they brought the gift and the card to the customer service counter and requested for gift wrapping and delivery.

On the day of the wedding, the guests were delighted to see the couple. Angela looked gorgeous in her beautiful white gown. Everyone was ushered into a huge room with many chairs lined up in rows. Right at the front of the room was a long table. The couple exchanged their vows and everyone congratulated them.

After the ceremony, everyone adjourned to a nearby hotel for the wedding party. The guests were treated to a sumptuous lunch. A live band performed while the bride and groom danced. It was a lovely wedding indeed!

23.title: The Leaf-tailed Gecko
23.text:
Dear Janice,

Look at the photograph on this postcard! Do you know what it is? It is impossible to play 'hide-and-seek' with this leaf-tailed gecko. It is capable of changing its colour. while on the branch of a tree, it remains so still and cleverly camouflaged that you will not notice it at all if you do not look hard enough.

With predators such as the snake and hawk, the leaf-tailed gecko certainly needs this natural ability to disguise itself. throughout the day, the leaf-tailed gecko hardly moves. But when threatened, it will try to frighten its attacker away as much as possible. It is only about twenty-eight centimetres long but it makes itself look bigger and fiercer by opening its mouth wide to show a red buccal cavity. It also makes a squawking noise to intimidate its enemy. if all these fail to deter the enemy, it drops its tail as a last resort.

The leaf-tailed gecko is a hunter too. It creeps around its habitat after dark and preys on small frogs, moths, beetles and other creepy-crawlies.

Isn't it interesting? I will be back in Singapore in a few days. I will catch up with you then. Take care!

Yours truly,
Elizabeth

24.title: Lucy the Lizard
24.text:
Lucy the lizard was pacing up and down the kitchen tiles. Just then, Wallace the cat emerged from nowhere and grabbed Lucy's tail. in order to save her own life, Lucy reacted quickly to the circumstances. She pulled herself away from Wallace, leaving her tail behind. Her tail twitched on the ground as though it had a life of its own. Wallace stopped to stare at it. although Lucy made her escape, she could not believe her tail was gone. She was embarrassed and so she decided to borrow a tail from one of her friends.

Lucy came to a big tree and saw Janet the dove in her nest, feeding her babies. She climbed up the tree trunk and crawled towards the end of the branch where Janet was. Lucy asked to borrow Janet's tail but was turned down. then Janet explained to Lucy that she needed the tail for good balance. moreover, her tail served as a rudder for navigation when she was flying and it acted as a brake too. Lucy nodded. She understood and climbed down the tree.

Lucy returned home looking extremely sad. Her mother found out what had happened and told her not to worry as she would soon grow another tail. True enough, a month later, Lucy noticed a new tail had grown and it was just like the last one she had!

25.title: The Sloth
25.text:
The sloth, the lethargic mammal of the animal kingdom, is a fascinating creature known for its leisurely movements. Found in the lush rainforests of Central and South America, its captivating charm has made it a subject of intrigue for animal enthusiasts all over the world.

Sloths predominantly inhabit the tropical rainforests of Central and South America, spanning countries like Costa Rica, Panama, Brazil and Venezuela. They thrive in the canopy, where they find safety from ground-dwelling predators. Sloths are arboreal creatures, often found lounging in the treetops. Their habitats offer them a constant supply of leaves for their peculiar diet.

although herbivores primarily consisting of leaves, they have a slow metabolic rate. Their digestive system is specialised to extract nutrients from the tough fibrous leaves they consume. Interestingly, the leaves they eat provide them with a minimal energy intake, which explains their sluggish pace and extended rest periods.

Sloths spend up to twenty hours a day resting or sleeping. They are excellent climbers and utilise their sharp claws for a secure grip on tree branches. When they do decide to move, it is at a very slow pace, which is one of their defining characteristics.

Sloths are solitary animals, and their fur often hosts a diverse ecosystem of algae and insects.

26.title: Fossils
26.text:
Fossils are the remains or traces of ancient plants and animals that have been preserved in rocks. They tell us about the vast number of species that existed millions of years ago on earth. They also reveal the development of various species over the years.

Fossils can be mineralised bones, teeth, shells, wood or actual unaltered material from a frozen organism like its fur. They are called body fossils. Eggs, nests, footprints, leaf impressions and dung are some examples of trace fossils which record the movement or behaviour of an organism or the appearance of a plant. One thing all fossils have in common is that they are at least 10 000 years old. Remains or traces of life are preserved when they get buried by sand, mud and clay brought about by the wind or water. In this way, they are protected from total destruction.

Paleontologists, people who specialise in the study of fossils, usually look for fossils in sedimentary rocks. They look out for unusual shapes and textures such as objects that are clearly different from the rocks around them. They take their time and work slowly and carefully to clean and uncover the fossils they have found. They need to handle their find with care as it may be fragile. They also take note of the location of their find because it may be an important historical site. The tools used to find fossils are neither fancy nor expensive. A butter knife and a toothbrush may be all an amateur paleontologist would need for a start.
